e.summary: **Design and pricing of a transparent parametric-modeled loss CAT bond**（arXiv `2609.22052v1`）**是一篇**把**「**透**明**的**触**发**机**制」**当**成 **CAT bond** 设计**核心**的**论文****——**逐字标题**为**「**Design and pricing of a transparent parametric-modeled loss CAT bond: application to German windstorm**」**，**作者逐字 **`John Ery` 与 **`Erwan Koch`****。**本次实测**：**⭐ 提交日 **2026-09-18****（**窗口内）**、**摘要**实测 **1,458** 字符**、**记录**中**无 **DOI**、**无**期刊**信息**、**无**作者**备注**。**⭐⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**软件**包**注册处**面（**npm）＋**补**修**上轮未决的 **arXiv** 线」**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四处最值得看**：**① **它**把**巨灾**债券**的**设计**矛**盾**说**成**一**句**可**操**作**的**话****——**⭐ 逐字**：**「**We present a new type of cat bond addressing the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk.**」**，**并**逐字**点**出**行**业**障**碍**（**逐字**：**the lack of transparency of this asset class has been a significant obstacle**）**——**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**对 **RIAA** 最有用**：**⭐ 即**赔**付**型（**indemnity）**触**发**减**少**了**基**差**风险**但**引入**道**德**风险**与**理**赔**透**明**度**问**题**，**而**纯**参**数**化（**parametric）**触**发**反**过**来**——**⭐ 这**是**风**险**转**移**里**最**古**老**的**权**衡**，**而**本**文**的**贡**献**是**把**它**做**成**「**透**明**且**易**评**估」**的**中**间**形**态**；**② **它**的**触**发**机**制**由**一**个 **cost random field** 推**出**，**并**逐字**分**离**三**个**部**件****（**逐字**：**Our trigger is derived from a cost random field which separates the physical hazard, a vulnerability function and the exposure. This allows the trigger to take a flexible form between parametric and modeled loss, in case exposure is taken into account.**）**——**⭐ 即**「**灾**害**强**度 × **脆**弱**性 × **暴**露」**三**因**素**分**开**建**模**，**从**而**能**在**「**只看**灾**害」**与**「**看**到**损**失」**之间**调**节**；**③ **案**例**与**方**法**细**节**都**是**行**业**标**准**做**法****（**逐字**：**We present a case study based on historical windstorm events impacting Germany. Using wind speed data from historical storms, we fit a max-stable random field on a resolution which is standard in the reinsurance industry. The availability of industry loss and exposure data allows us to calibrate the vulnerability component to historical observations. Besides measuring the basis risk associated with our trigger, we perform a full model assessment and discuss numerical results.**）**——**⭐ 即**极**值**统**计**（**max-stable **random field）**＋**行**业**损**失**数**据**校**准**＋**基**差**风险**度**量**，**三**件**事**都**做**了**；**④ **它**的**受**众**逐字**同**时**包**含**「**保**险**人**与**公**共**部**门」**与**「**想**进**入 **CAT bond** 市场**的**新**参与**者」**——**⭐ 即**定**位**是**「**降**低**进入**门槛」**。**⚠️ 本次**未读**其**正文**、**未**复**现**其**任**何**定**价**或**基**差**风险**计**算**。
e.body:
**Design and pricing of a transparent parametric-modeled loss CAT bond**（arXiv `2609.22052v1`）**是一篇**把**「**透**明**的**触**发**机**制」**当**成 **CAT bond** 设计**核心**的**论文****——**逐字标题**为**「**Design and pricing of a transparent parametric-modeled loss CAT bond: application to German windstorm**」**，**作者逐字 **`John Ery` 与 **`Erwan Koch`****。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**软件**包**注册处**面（**npm）＋**补**修**上轮未决的 **arXiv** 线」**。
**可核实信息（均 2026-09-25 arXiv API 实测）**：
**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它**把 **CAT bond** 的**设计**矛**盾**写**成**一**句**可**操**作**的**话****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**摘要**逐字**写**「**Catastrophe (cat) bonds overcome some lack of reinsurance by sourcing capacity from the wider capital markets. We present a new type of cat bond addressing the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk.**」**，**并**逐字**点**出**行**业**障**碍**（**逐字**：**but also for players willing to enter the cat bond market for whom the lack of transparency of this asset class has been a significant obstacle**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**对 **RIAA** 最有用**：**⭐ 即**风**险**转**移**里**最**古**老**的**权**衡**——**赔**付**型（**indemnity）**触**发**贴**近**实**际**损**失**（**基**差**小）**，**但**需**要**理**赔**过**程**与**透**明**度**透**明**（**道**德**风险**与**信**息**不**对**称**大）**；**纯**参**数**化**触**发**透**明**、**易**估**值**，**但**与**实**际**损**失**脱**钩**（**基**差**大）**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**做**巨灾**或**参数**化**保险**作业**时**，**先**把**这**两**端**摆**出**来**，**再**谈**中**间**设**计**——**⭐ 而**这**篇**的**贡**献**正**是**一**个**「**透**明**且**易**评**估」**的**中**间**形**态**。
**⭐⭐ ② 它**的**触**发**机**制**由**一**个 **cost random field** 推**出**，**并**逐字**分**离**三**个**部**件****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**摘要**逐字**写**「**Our trigger is derived from a cost random field which separates the physical hazard, a vulnerability function and the exposure. This allows the trigger to take a flexible form between parametric and modeled loss, in case exposure is taken into account.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**「**灾**害**强**度 × **脆**弱**性 × **暴**露」**这**个**三**因**素**分**解**是**巨灾**建模**的**通**用**结**构**，**而**本**文**把**它**用**在**「**触**发**条**件**的**定**义」**上**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**做**参**数**化**产品**设计**时**，**把**「**只**看**灾**害」**与**「**看**到**损**失」**当**成**一**个**连**续**谱**而**不**是**二**选**一**，**并**说**明**自**己**停**在**哪**一**点**（**⭐ 案**例**逐字**为**「**the trigger can take a flexible form between parametric and modeled loss**」）**。
**⭐⭐ ③ 案**例**与**方**法**细**节**逐字**都**是**行**业**标**准**做**法****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**摘要**逐字**写**「**We present a case study based on historical windstorm events impacting Germany. Using wind speed data from historical storms, we fit a max-stable random field on a resolution which is standard in the reinsurance industry. The availability of industry loss and exposure data allows us to calibrate the vulnerability component to historical observations. Besides measuring the basis risk associated with our trigger, we perform a full model assessment and discuss numerical results.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**三**件**事**都**做**了**——**极**值**统计**（**max-stable **random field）**、**用**行**业**损**失**与**暴露**数**据**校**准**脆**弱**性**、**并**度**量**触**发**机**制**带**来**的**基**差**风险**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**这**是**「**新**触**发**设计**必**须**附**带**基**差**风险**度**量」**的**标**准**动**作**（**⭐ 与**第 **380** 轮**记下的**「**估**不**了**的**参**数**要**声明**并**做**网格**敏感**性」**同**属**「**把**不**利**结**果**也**报**出**来」**）。
**⭐⭐ ④ 它**的**受**众**定**位**逐字**同**时**含**三**类**角**色****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**摘要**逐字**写**「**This is relevant for insurers and public authorities in a world where natural disasters are occurring with increasing frequency and severity due to climate change, but also for players willing to enter the cat bond market**」**；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**它**把**「**降**低**进入**门槛」**写**成**动**机**（**针**对**因**透**明**度**不**足**而**观**望**的**新**参与**者）**，**而**不**只**是**对**已**有**再**保**买家**说话**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**写**产品**或**研究**动机**时**，**指**明**「**谁**因**为**什么**障**碍**而**没**有**用**上**这**个**工**具」**，**通**常**比**「**提**升**效**率」**更**有**说服**力**。
**⭐⭐ ⑤ 元数据**形态**与**引**用**口径****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**逐字**给出 **id **`http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22052v1`**、**published 与 **updated 均 **2026-09-18**、**作者 **`John Ery`** 与 **`Erwan Koch`**、**`arxiv:comment`／**`arxiv:doi`／**`arxiv:journal_ref`** 三**个**字**段**均**为**空**、**摘要**实测 **1,458** 字符**；**⭐ 本词条**如实**指出**：**⭐ 即**它**是**一**篇**尚**未**见**期**刊**信**息**的**预**印**本**（**⭐ 与**本**轮**另**一**条**同**形）**——**故**引用**时**要**写**明**版**本**与**时**点**。
**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[cat-bond-pricing]] 覆盖**巨灾**债券**定价**、**[[catastrophe-modeler]] 覆盖**巨灾**建模**工具**、**[[geo-catastrophe-pricing]] 覆盖**地理**维**度**的**巨灾**定价**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**以**透明**触**发**机**制**在**参数**化**与**模拟**损失**之间**取**中**间**形态」这一**形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。
**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 五件事值得借**：**① **先**摆**出**道**德**风险**与**基**差**风险**两**端**；**② **把**触**发**写**成**「**灾**害 × **脆**弱**性 × **暴露」**的**连**续**谱**；**③ **新**触**发**必**附**基**差**风险**度**量**；**④ **动**机**写**成**「**谁**因**何**障**碍**而**未**用」**；**⑤ **引**用**预**印**本**写**明**版**本**与**时**点**。
**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有阅读**其**正文**、**未**复**现**其**定**价**方**法**、**触**发**机**制**或**基**差**风险**计**算**，**故**不**主张**其**方**法**正确**性**、**定**价**结果**或**基**差**风险**度**量**的**可信度**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**arXiv** 记录**接口**返回的**元数据与摘要**（**摘要**实测 **1,458** 字符）**，**未读**其**全文**。**③ ⚠️ **未核实**其**是**否**已**投**稿**或**发**表**（**记录**中 **`arxiv:doi`** 与 **`arxiv:journal_ref`** 均**为**空）**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**所**用**行**业**损**失**与**暴露**数**据**的**来**源**与**授**权**（**摘要**只**说 **`The availability of industry loss and exposure data`）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其 **max-stable** 随**机**场**的**分**辨**率**与**拟**合**细**节**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核实**其**是**否**附**带**代**码**或**数**据**。**⑦ ⚠️ 窗口**状况**：**提交日 **2026-09-18** 落在**本轮**窗口**之内**（**基准日 **2026-09-25）**，**故**无需**缺口**说明**。**⑧ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-25 所见**；**⚠️ 涉**及**巨灾**债券**与**参数**化**保险**，**⚠️ 不**构成**任何**投**资**、**定**价**或**产品**设计**意见**。

We present a new type of cat bond addressing the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk. 与 As our main contributions we propose a trigger mechanism which is entirely transparent and simpler to evaluate compared to indemnity modeling techniques, as well as a methodology to price this cat bond. 与 This is relevant for insurers and public authorities in a world where natural disasters are occurring with increasing frequency and severity due to climate change, but also for players willing to enter the cat bond market for whom the lack of transparency of this asset class has been a significant obstacle. 与 Our trigger is derived from a cost random field which separates the physical hazard, a vulnerability function and the exposure. e.title_en: A paper that makes a transparent trigger mechanism the core of catastrophe bond design: it addresses the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk, identifies the lack of transparency of the asset class as a significant obstacle for entrants, derives its trigger from a cost random field that separates physical hazard, a vulnerability function, and exposure so that the trigger can take a flexible form between parametric and modelled loss, and presents a case study on historical windstorm events affecting one country using a max-stable random field at a resolution standard in the reinsurance industry.

e.summary_en: This paper makes a transparent trigger mechanism the core of catastrophe bond design, and its title names a transparent parametric-modelled loss bond applied to windstorm in one country. **Measured this round**: submitted on the eighteenth of September inside the window by two authors, with an abstract of about fifteen hundred characters, and with no archival identifier, journal reference, or author note in the record. **This round theme is the package registry surface together with fixing the preprint surface left unresolved in an earlier round.** **Four things are worth reading: it states the design tension of catastrophe bonds in one operational sentence, presenting a bond type that addresses the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk, and naming the lack of transparency of the asset class as a significant obstacle for players wishing to enter that market, which matters because indemnity triggers reduce basis risk but introduce moral hazard and loss-adjustment transparency problems while purely parametric triggers do the opposite, making this the oldest trade-off in risk transfer, and the contribution is an intermediate form that is both transparent and simpler to evaluate; its trigger is derived from a cost random field that separates three components, namely the physical hazard, a vulnerability function, and the exposure, which lets the trigger take a flexible form between parametric and modelled loss once exposure is taken into account, so hazard intensity, vulnerability, and exposure are modelled separately and the design can slide between looking only at the hazard and looking all the way to loss; its case study and method details follow industry-standard practice, fitting a max-stable random field to historical wind speeds at a resolution standard in the reinsurance industry, calibrating the vulnerability component to historical observations using industry loss and exposure data, and measuring the basis risk of the trigger alongside a full model assessment; and its stated audience includes insurers and public authorities as well as new entrants, positioning it as lowering the barrier to entry.** **The paper text was not read and none of its pricing or basis risk computations were reproduced this round.**

e.body_en:
This paper makes a transparent trigger mechanism the core of catastrophe bond design. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the package registry surface together with fixing the preprint surface left unresolved in an earlier round.**
**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-25 from the preprint interface**:
**First, it states the design tension of catastrophe bonds in one operational sentence.** The abstract says that catastrophe bonds overcome some lack of reinsurance capacity by sourcing from wider capital markets, that the paper presents a new bond type addressing the known trade-off between moral hazard and basis risk, and that a lack of transparency in this asset class has been a significant obstacle for players wishing to enter that market. **Indemnity triggers sit close to actual loss so basis risk is small, but they require loss adjustment and bring moral hazard and information asymmetry, while purely parametric triggers are transparent and easy to value but detach from actual loss, which is the oldest trade-off in risk transfer. Catastrophe or parametric insurance coursework should lay out both ends before discussing an intermediate design, which is exactly what this paper contributes.**
**Second, its trigger is derived from a cost random field that separates three components.** The abstract states that the trigger separates the physical hazard, a vulnerability function, and the exposure, which lets the trigger take a flexible form between parametric and modelled loss once exposure is taken into account. **Hazard intensity times vulnerability times exposure is the general structure of catastrophe modelling, and this paper applies it to the definition of the trigger condition, so parametric product design should treat looking only at the hazard and looking all the way to loss as a continuum rather than a binary choice, and should state where it stops.**
**Third, the case study and method details follow industry-standard practice.** The abstract reports a case study on historical windstorms affecting one country, fitting a max-stable random field to historical wind speed data at a resolution standard in the reinsurance industry, calibrating the vulnerability component to historical observations using available industry loss and exposure data, and measuring the basis risk of the trigger alongside a full model assessment. **Attaching a basis risk measurement to any new trigger design is the standard move, in the same family as the earlier note that an unestimable parameter should be declared and given a sensitivity grid, since both report the unflattering part as well.**
**Fourth, its stated audience spans three kinds of reader.** The abstract says the work is relevant for insurers and public authorities in a world of increasingly frequent and severe natural disasters due to climate change, and also for players willing to enter the catastrophe bond market. **Framing the motivation as lowering a barrier that keeps a specific group out is usually more persuasive than claiming efficiency gains, and it is a framing worth copying in product or research motivation sections.**
**Fifth, metadata shape and citation convention.** The record gives an identifier, submission and update dates in the window, two named authors, empty fields for the author comment, archival identifier, and journal reference, and an abstract of about fifteen hundred characters. **This is a preprint with no journal information visible yet, the same shape as another entry this round, so citations should state the version and the date of access.**
**Sixth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover catastrophe bond pricing, catastrophe modelling tools, and geographically oriented catastrophe pricing, **while this entry supplies the form of a trigger design that slides between parametric and modelled loss by separating hazard, vulnerability, and exposure. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**
**For RIAA**: **five practices transfer: state both ends of the moral hazard and basis risk trade-off first; write the trigger as a continuum over hazard, vulnerability, and exposure; attach a basis risk measurement to any new trigger; frame the motivation around who is excluded by which barrier; and state version and access date when citing a preprint.**
**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the paper text was not read and none of its pricing method, trigger mechanism, or basis risk computation was reproduced**, so no claim is made about correctness, pricing results, or the credibility of the basis risk measurement. **Second, only metadata and abstract, measured at about fifteen hundred characters, were read**, not the full text. **Third, whether it has been submitted or published was not verified**, the archival identifier and journal reference fields being empty. **Fourth, the provenance and licensing of the industry loss and exposure data were not verified**, the abstract only referring to their availability. **Fifth, the resolution and fitting details of the max-stable random field were not verified. Sixth, whether code or data accompany it was not verified. Seventh, the submission date falls inside this round window against a baseline of the twenty-fifth of September. Eighth, this entry records what was visible on that date and states plainly that it constitutes no investment, pricing, or product design opinion.**
